controls: SQL injection
Keep typed data separate from database commands.
verified
ORM predicates bind data; dynamic sorting and maintenance identifiers use fixed allowlists.
No independent penetration test; future raw SQL needs the same review.
Cross-site scripting (XSS)
Stop saved text from becoming a browser script.
verified
React renders user text as text; links are validated, PDF previews are raster images and a restrictive CSP blocks scripts.
XSS on a trusted origin can still read memory; these cases do not prove all future views safe.
Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
Stop another website from submitting actions through a browser.
verified
Every mutating API call requires X-BuildTrust-Request: 1; browser Origin and Fetch Metadata are checked before business handling. No auth cookies.
An allowed-origin script remains trusted; a stolen bearer token is not prevented by CSRF controls.
File upload validation
Accept bounded supported documents and retain their evidence.
verified
Signatures, allowed types, body/file size, archive expansion, pages, child deadlines and private paths are bounded. Procurement remains untrusted until confirmed.
No antivirus or complete malware-sandbox claim; human evidence can still be false.
Server-side request forgery (SSRF)
Keep outbound connections within intended destinations.
verified
Provider requests allow exact HTTPS hosts and ports, no credentials or redirects, and ignore environment proxies. Ollama is explicitly loopback-only. Listing URLs are never fetched.
Paid/live providers and a real local model retain separate external acceptance.
Object-level authorization
Check which project owns every requested record.
verified
Current account and project membership are checked through shared resource helpers, including child records and protected files.
This is application isolation, not native SQLite RLS or protection against an unrestricted DB owner.
Rate limiting
Bound repeated sign-ins and expensive operations.
verified
Persistent account/IP admission limits and operation budgets include MFA verification and management. Challenges allow five failed codes.
Shared local IPs may share admission limits; this is a single-process local release.
Password hashing
Store a slow password hash instead of the password.
verified
Argon2 hashes protect private passwords. Password checks run outside ordinary financial writer locks.
Public-demo passwords are intentionally public; offline setup needs OS protection.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
Require a password and an authenticator for privileged private users.
verified
Private Admin/Finance MFA is mandatory; optional roles may enroll. TOTP factors are encrypted, challenges/codes hashed, replay rejected and recovery use atomic. Only the owner resets lost factors.
Local automated TOTP and browser evidence is not an independent phone/interoperability or phishing-resistance assessment. Public demo is exempt.
Server-side permissions
Check whether the current role may perform the action.
verified
Every protected request reloads current account, role, membership and session assurance; financial execution revalidates sources and approval.
OS/database owner remains trusted. The copilot cannot approve or settle.
Native row-level security (RLS)
Let the database itself enforce row-access policies.
deferred
SQLite uses server-side project predicates. Native database RLS has not been enabled.
Deferred: a future PostgreSQL migration needs native policies and acceptance.
JWT signing secrets
Prevent forged or stale server sessions.
verified
Private random JWT keys must contain at least 32 UTF-8 bytes; existing strong keys are retained. Signed tokens also need an active server session and MFA assurance when applicable.
An unrestricted host owner can read signing material; TLS is required before any remote deployment.
Server-only API secrets
Keep provider credentials outside the browser and public source.
verified
API credentials and separate MFA encryption keys stay in protected server storage and private backups; paid dispatch is off by default.
No genuine exposed provider key was found; unavailable provider ownership would still block a required rotation.
No persistent browser tokens
Avoid leaving credentials in browser storage.
verified
Access tokens, restricted challenges, setup keys and recovery codes remain in memory. Only harmless view filters may persist.
A page refresh requires sign-in; memory storage alone cannot defeat XSS.
Tight CORS and trusted origins
Allow the intended local browser application only.
verified
Cross-origin access is disabled. Trusted hosts and browser origins are explicit per launcher; forwarded headers do not define trust.
A future hosted address needs deliberate configuration and HTTPS review.
Webhook signatures
Authenticate incoming integration callbacks before processing them.
not applicable
No incoming webhook integration or real payment callback exists; callbacks remain disabled.
Not applicable now. Any future webhook needs provider-specific signatures and replay controls.
Production source maps
Do not publish browser debug maps with the running app.
verified
Production source maps are explicitly disabled. API/static handling rejects .map requests.
Public source is intentionally available under AGPL; hiding maps is not an access-control boundary.
Logs and lockfile hygiene
Keep private values out of diagnostics and dependency records.
verified
Errors are generic with request IDs; structured logs omit tokens, passwords and content. Lockfiles and nested archives are included in redacted secret scans.
Pattern scans cannot guarantee discovery of every possible secret format.
Dependency vulnerabilities
Check published advisories and install reproducible versions.
verified
Reproducible locks include maintained MFA libraries with attribution. Known-advisory scans cover Python and frontend dependencies.
New vulnerabilities can appear; this is not a complete supply-chain or penetration assessment.
